context_documents.title: 2025-111 · Floor supply changes the mechanism without replacing the scoring arm
context_documents.body:
# 2025-111: Floor supply changes the mechanism without replacing the scoring arm

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A floor collector was added after Northern Lights while the elevator/arm architecture remained. The retained account identifies roughly 16 pounds of added collector mass, offset by lighter carriage/effector parts. Internal rollers retain coral while the mechanism holds it inverted during algae acquisition. Coral and algae contact regions are offset by about six inches.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly identifies difficult station alignment under defense and successful floor pickups on 1778/2046 as motivations. The offset is described as allowing algae removal and coral placement in one fluid transition.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A floor collector should be evaluated as a new cycle source, not an isolated pickup demo. The existing arm must keep coral controlled through the algae motion, and mass must be recovered elsewhere without creating excessive compliance. The six-inch separation is an interface dimension for that combined motion; it is not a universal clearance between any two manipulators.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare defended station cycles with complete floor-to-score cycles, including failed pickups and inverted retention. Check whether the mass-saving parts preserve L4 accuracy and fatigue life.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
